title: Storage: object, block and file systems

videos.script: Ask where a server keeps its files, and most people picture a disk inside the machine. {{disk}} In a cloud, three different services hide behind the word storage, and they are not three sizes of disk. A block volume is a disk your operating system formats, attached over the network to one machine. A file service is a shared directory that many machines mount at once. An object store is neither. You hand it whole files over HTTP and ask for them back by name. {{three}} Each one is addressed differently, fails differently and is priced differently. Take five hundred gigabytes, kept in São Paulo for a month, at the public list price. As objects they cost about twenty dollars. As a volume, seventy-six. As a shared file system, two hundred and eighty-five. {{prices}} This lesson works out where those differences come from. You will make a bucket on a laptop program that imitates the S3 interface, put two files in it, and watch a rename turn into a copy and a delete. {{bucket}} Then come storage classes, lifecycle rules and versioning. They decide what old data costs, and whether a file somebody deleted can come back. {{versions}} The lesson ends with a table for choosing, and with the reason so many buckets end up public. {{choose}}
